speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start after a specific injury or event?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

Given your year-long history of burning pain and paresthesias, combined with recent progressive bilateral hand weakness, this strongly suggests cervical myelopathy. I need to confirm if you are experiencing gait disturbances, loss of fine motor skills like buttoning shirts, or bowel/bladder changes. Also, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your legs?
